answer: A summit-level reputation ledger resists Sybil attacks by pricing identity through verifiable work: an agent earns trust only by completing checked tasks over time, so a hollow identity with no history carries no weight. New agents start on a mesa of limited privilege — small transactions only — and climb gradually. Cloning thousands of identities is free, but none can spend or vote until each accumulates costly, checkable work, making a fake army expensive and useless.
